questions.q: To which place did the man then bring Ezekiel?
questions.a: The man then brought Ezekiel to the gate that opened to the east.

questions.q: What did Ezekiel see and from what direction did it come?
questions.a: Ezekiel saw the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east.

questions.q: What did Ezekiel do when he saw the appearance of the glory?
questions.a: Ezekiel threw himself face down on the ground to worship.

questions.q: By which gate did the glory of Yahweh come to the house?
questions.a: The glory of Yahweh came to the house by the gate that faces east.

questions.q: How did Ezekiel get to the inner courtyard?
questions.a: A wind lifted Ezekiel up and brought him to the inner courtyard.

questions.q: From where did Ezekiel hear someone speaking to him?
questions.a: Ezekiel heard someone speaking to him from inside the temple building.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel do to dishonor Yahweh that they would no longer do in this temple?
questions.a: They used to do many disgusting things that dishonored Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would do in the temple in the vision?
questions.a: Yahweh said that this is where he will rule as king, and he will live among the people of Israel there forever.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would do if the people of Israel stop doing these bad things?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would make himself present with them forever.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to do about the temple he had seen in the vision?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to describe this temple he had seen in the vision to the people of Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say about this temple area on the top of the mountain?
questions.a: Yahweh said that the whole area around the top of the mountain is most holy.

questions.q: What kind of cubit did the man use to measure the altar?
questions.a: The man used a measurement that was a cubit and a handbreadth long.

questions.q: How high was the lower ledge of the altar above the ground?
questions.a: The lower ledge was two cubits or 1.1 meters above the ground.

questions.q: What things point upward from the hearth?
questions.a: Four horns point upward from the hearth.

questions.q: How long and how wide was the hearth?
questions.a: The hearth was 12 cubits long and 12 cubits wide.

questions.q: On which side of the altar were the steps?
questions.a: The steps were on the east side of the altar.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say the priests would do on the altar on the day it was made?
questions.a: Yahweh said the priests would offer a burnt offering on the altar and splash blood on it.

questions.q: Whose descendants would serve as the Levitical priests at this altar?
questions.a: The descendants of Zadok would serve as Levitical priests at this altar.

questions.q: What would placing the blood on the altar do for it?
questions.a: Placing the blood on the altar would cleanse it and make it pure.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say should be done with the bull of the sin offering?
questions.a: Yahweh said the bull should be burned in the appointed place outside the sacred area.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say should be presented as the sin offering on the second day?
questions.a: Yahweh said a male goat without imperfections should be offered as a sin offering on the second day.

questions.q: What animals did Yahweh say to present after they finished purifying of the altar?
questions.a: Yahweh said to present a bull and a ram, both without imperfections.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say the priests should throw on the animals?
questions.a: Yahweh said the priests should throw salt on the animals.

questions.q: What would the priests have to do for seven days as a purifying sacrifice?
questions.a: The priests would have to offer a male goat as a sin offering each day, along with an unblemished bull and an unblemished ram.

questions.q: On the eighth day and onward, what did Yahweh declare he would do?
questions.a: Yahweh declared that he would accept the people after the priests offered their burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar.

commentary.text: After Ezekiel had surveyed the temple of God, he had a vision of the glory of God. When Christ crucified, and the things freely given to us of God, through Him, are shown to us by the Holy Ghost, they make us ashamed for our sins. This frame of mind prepares us for fuller discoveries of the mysteries of redeeming love; and the whole of the Scriptures should be opened and applied, that men may see their sins, and repent of them. We are not now to offer any atoning sacrifices, for by one offering Christ has perfected for ever those that are sanctified, Heb. 10:14; but the sprinkling of his blood is needful in all our approaches to God the Father. Our best services can be accepted only as sprinkled with the blood which cleanses from all sin.
